name: EvoSkill
institution: Sentient (Sentient Labs) and Virginia Tech; authors Salaheddin Alzubi, Noah Provenzano, Jaydon Bingham, Weiyuan Chen, Tu Vu
type: industry (open-source engineering framework with accompanying preprint)
what_evolved: Context (memory & prompts) and Tools/skills; whole agent program = system prompt + skill set. Model weights remain frozen. Extends GEPA's single-file prompt optimization to joint skill+prompt mutation producing a new agent program each iteration.
skill_as_artifact: Yes. Skills are independent reusable artifacts packaged as folders containing SKILL-style instructions (markdown), metadata, and helper scripts. Cross-agent compatible (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, OpenHands, Goose, Harbor). Stored under .claude/skills/ and versioned on git branches.
skill_encoding: Hybrid: natural-language skill documents (.md instructions) plus executable helper code/scripts inside each skill folder; program configuration in .claude/program.yaml (system prompt, tools, score).
skill_granularity: Sub-task workflow and reusable code/policy rules for domain-specific capabilities (e.g. data extraction, search/retrieval workflows); each skill targets a recurring failure pattern rather than atomic actions.
how_method: rollout_optimization (non-gradient, textual feedback) combined with population_evolutionary selection. Five-stage loop: Base Agent runs current best program -> Proposer analyzes failure trajectories and proposes targeted skill/prompt edits -> Generator writes new skill files or rewrites system prompt -> Evaluator scores on held-out validation -> Frontier keeps top-N programs as git branches. Pareto-frontier selection retains only programs that improve held-out performance; multiple skill and prompt mutations are proposed jointly per iteration (vs GEPA's single in-place prompt revision).
learning_signal_source: Failure trajectories (failed rollouts analyzed by Proposer) and held-out validation accuracy (outcome reward). Scorer configurable: string/exact match, numeric tolerance, LLM-as-judge rubric, custom script, or Harbor built-in verifier.
reward_granularity: outcome (validation-set accuracy after full rollout drives frontier selection), with process-level failure analysis feeding the proposer.
learning_paradigm: offline; on-policy (each iteration's rollouts use the current best/frontier program). Loop runs as a batch self-improvement process, not during task serving. [uncertain]
when_evolve: inter-test-time (offline self-improvement loop run on a benchmark/held-out dataset between deployments, not intra-task online).
trigger: failure-driven (proposer targets failed cases) within a periodic/configurable iteration loop (default 20 iterations, frontier_size 3, no_improvement_limit 5). User-invoked via `evoskill run`; continuous/usage-driven evolution is an open research direction.
library_structure: Versioned skill library on git branches: `program/base`, `program/iter-skill-*` with `frontier/*` tags marking top-N programs. Skills live as folders under `.claude/skills/`; program config in `.claude/program.yaml`. EvoSkill only writes to `program/`-prefixed branches. Flat skill-folder layout with frontier-based selection (not hierarchical/vector DB).
retrieval_method: Generation-as-retrieval: the Proposer analyzes failures and generates targeted new skills or edits; skills are then directly reused as agent context (loaded into system prompt / skills directory) and packaged for cross-agent/cross-model transfer. No semantic vector retrieval.
validation: Held-out validation set with validation gating (new variant only enters frontier if it beats current best on held-out data). Execution-based scoring via configurable scorers (exact, multi-tolerance, LLM-judge, script, Harbor verifier). `evoskill eval` re-scores best program on validation set.
error_correction: Self-revision via Proposer/Generator loop that rewrites skills/prompts in response to failures; bounded edits enforced by frontier selection (worse-performing variants are discarded, never entering the frontier). `evoskill diff` and `--continue` support inspection and resumption.
test_env: coding / QA tool-call environments: OfficeQA (grounded reasoning over U.S. Treasury data), SealQA (search-augmented QA with noisy retrieval), BrowseComp (zero-shot transfer), SWE-bench-verified (containerized via Harbor), and arbitrary user CSV/Harbor benchmarks.
backbone_model: Model-agnostic and frozen: Claude (Sonnet 4.6), GPT-5/o3, GLM, Minimax, Kimi, Gemini, Qwen, Llama (Fireworks). Any provider via OpenRouter/Anthropic/OpenAI/Fireworks. Demonstrated cross-model transfer of evolved skills.
where_deploy: general (turns general-purpose coding agents into specialists); validated on coding, document QA, and web-search QA domains.
metrics: success_rate (exact-match / verifier accuracy), generalization (zero-shot cross-task and cross-model transfer), skill_library_growth (frontier size, skills discovered), cost (LLM calls per iteration, run wall-time).
key_results: OfficeQA exact-match +7.3% (60.6% -> 67.9%); SealQA +12.1% (26.6% -> 38.7%); zero-shot transfer of SealQA-evolved skills to BrowseComp +5.3% without modification; demonstrated cross-model, cross-agent, and cross-task transferability of evolved skill folders.
limitations: Continuous (usage-driven) evolution and evolution-without-a-benchmark are open/in-progress research directions (currently needs a held-out benchmark + verifier). Runs take hours (mitigated by Docker/Daytona remote exec). Potential eval-hacking risk from frontier selection on held-out data. Transferability bounded to skill-level (model weights frozen). Controllability depends on task.md and scorer quality.
